title: Finite-type torsion morphisms satisfy the universal nearby-cycle finiteness condition
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\geq1$, and let $g:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a geometric point $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], write $X_{(x)}$ and $Y_{(g(x))}$ for the strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $g_{(x)}:X_{(x)}\to Y_{(g(x))}$ for the induced morphism. Direct images are on the small etale module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then $g$ satisfies condition (*) universally, meaning the following precise assertion: for every base change $g':X'=X\times_YY'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there is an open covering $X'=\bigcup_\alpha U_\alpha$ and integers $N_\alpha\geq0$ such that for every geometric point $x'$ of $U_\alpha$, every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X'_{(x')}$, and every $q>N_\alpha$, one has $R^qg'_{(x')*}F=0$.

source.place: Definition A.1 and the sentence before Remark A.2, p. 1 (Gabber finiteness, cited there as [O, Proposition 3.1] and [I, Corollary 1.15]); local PDF WANTED.
